integrity: The exact neighbor-only model is analyzed; finite rational checks and floating-point diagnostics supplement an analytic asymptotic proof. No independent audit or external certification is claimed.
limitations: Proves expected consensus time on complete simple social networks at fixed bias 1/9; does not prove distributional limits, noncomplete-network behavior, or bias-perturbation uniformity. Mathematical probability methods are used to analyze a social opinion-update mechanism.
title: Critical \(n^{4/3}\) consensus law at the biased two-choices threshold
